Memory items from past tasks:
- [rb-0010] Check idempotency key before any state validation: When implementing money-moving operations, look up the idempotency key in the audit trail first and return the original result early, before validating payment state or amounts.
  Scan audit.events(<event_name>) for a matching idempotency_key at the very top of the function and return the original record unchanged. Doing this before state checks prevents spurious errors on retries (e.g. a payment already 'refunded' would otherwise fail the captured-state check).
- [rb-0016] Check idempotency key before state validation: When adding idempotency to money-moving operations, look up the audit log for the key before validating payment state or applying changes.
  Iterate audit.events(<event_type>) for an entry whose idempotency_key matches; if found, return the original result (the same record for record-returning functions) immediately. Only after the key check should you validate state and mutate, so retries of an already-applied operation succeed instead of raising invalid_state.
- [rb-0012] Use money helpers and float for audit amounts: Normalize amounts with to_money/round_money, compare against ZERO, and write float(amount) into audit entries because the ledger JSON importer rejects Decimal.
  Convert inputs via round_money(to_money(amount)), reject non-positive amounts, and accumulate refunded_amount with the same rounding. Always pass float(amount) (and float of running totals) to audit.record to satisfy the ledger service importer.
- [rb-0017] Add keyword-only idempotency_key to payment operations: Team convention requires every operation that moves money or changes a payment/credit/invoice balance to accept an optional keyword-only idempotency_key=None.
  Signature pattern: def capture(payment, at, *, idempotency_key=None). Callers without a key must keep working, so default to None and skip the lookup when it is None. Include idempotency_key in the audit.record call you write.
- [rb-0011] Inspect sibling modules for undocumented team conventions: The first attempt missed idempotency_key, approved_by, and float(amount) audit conventions that were visible in existing modules like payments.py and audit.py.
  Before implementing a new function, read analogous functions in sibling modules (payments.py, audit.py) to infer required keyword-only params, error codes, and audit field formats. These conventions are often not stated in the issue but are enforced by hidden tests.
- [rb-0009] Handle edge cases explicitly in interval queries: Guard against invalid periods and queries before the start time when computing the next occurrence.
  Raise BillingError for period_days <= 0, and when after < start return start + length (the first renewal) rather than relying on floor division, which would otherwise produce a non-positive index.

    return round_money(sum((line_total(line) for line in invoice.lines), ZERO))

        raise BillingError("invalid_state", f"invoice {invoice.id} is {invoice.status}")

        raise BillingError("empty_invoice", invoice.id)
    invoice.issued_at = ensure_utc(at)
    invoice.status = "issued"
    audit.record("invoice_issued", invoice_id=invoice.id, total=invoice_total(invoice))
    return invoice
